question: Is EA's 1.3.1.0 Claymore figure (fragmentation base close-range damage 65 to 50) stored, given that the blast object holds BlastDamage 1?

sourceFacts.method: M18Claymore_Projectile was decoded and every boxed named value listed (boxed.py). One object (Class_1788e77e) holds a list of eight name-hash and value pairs; its three non-zero floats were located in the raw file and checked. No registry row is named for the Claymore's damage (18 Claymore rows, all for the weapon blueprint).

control.description: The blast object of the same file reads InnerBlastRadius 2.5, BlastDamage 1, BlastRadius 5, as already recorded (GADGET_SITE_ADDITIONS.md, L164).

sourceFacts.eaStatement: Updated the M18A1 Claymore fragmentation base close range damage from 65 to 50. Damage drop-off now starts at the edge of the detection arc.
sourceFacts.note: Name hashes are of stripped property names; the three differ only in their low bytes (2b715869, 2b71592f, 2b7158ae), which suggests three names of one family.

inference: The value 50 is the only stored 50 tied to the Claymore's damage and equals EA's new close-range figure. It is a correspondence: the property name is a hash and no consumer was traced.
The neighbouring values 30 and 15 belong to the same family of names. A reading as far damage 30 and a distance of 15 m is a guess and is not recorded as a value.
The Claymore's damage is therefore not in its blast object (BlastDamage 1) but in this property list, which explains why earlier leads could not give it a damage figure.
unresolved: Names and meaning of the three values. Test: stand in front of an enemy Claymore at 1 m (50 expected) and at the edge of its range, reading health lost.
EA's old value 65 is not in the file.
siteImpact: None. No Analyzer data, simulation or UI change.

leads.title: Claymore: a named value of 50 in the projectile's property list equals EA's fragmentation close-range damage; its neighbours 30 and 15 are unnamed
leads.summary: The Claymore's projectile file holds three named values, 30, 50 and 15, in a property list separate from its blast object (BlastDamage 1). The 50 equals EA's 1.3.1.0 fragmentation close-range damage; the names are hashes and the other two values are unread. 3 raw-offset checks matched.
leads.reopenWhen: The property names are resolved or an in-game Claymore damage reading.
leads.statusNote: Value 50 found and matches EA; meaning by correspondence only.
